name: site/mineral-strip
title: MineralStrip
summary: The decorative seven-mineral accent bar: a full-height ~6px strip fixed to the left edge of the page, in seven equal segments coloured cobalt, tanzanite, malachite, gold, terracotta, sodalite and copper, top to bottom.

props.name: ...attributes
props.description: None: the component takes no props and forwards no attributes. Listed this way because the .astro declares no `interface Props`, which the Astro runner reads as attribute pass-through.

behaviour: Renders one <div class="mineral-strip" data-slot="mineral-strip" aria-hidden="true"> holding seven empty <span data-mineral="<mineral>">, in the order cobalt, tanzanite, malachite, gold, terracotta, sodalite, copper.
Its own stylesheet fixes it to the left edge (6px wide, 100dvh tall, z-index 50, pointer-events none) and colours each segment by its data-mineral from the `--color-<mineral>` custom property.
No inline style attribute: the segments are coloured by attribute selector, so a page's CSP can keep `style-src 'self'`.

keyboard: None: it is decorative and never focusable.
aria: aria-hidden="true": it never reaches the accessibility tree.

theming.brandOverlay: Nothing: the strip is the seven minerals in a fixed order on every brand. They are named only as data-mineral attributes and in the component's stylesheet, never as colour classes.

noJs.without: Everything: the component is server-rendered HTML and CSS with no script.

responsive: The same 6px full-height strip at every width; it does not take layout space (position fixed), so content must leave room for it.
contract:
contract
  slot is "mineral-strip"
  class contains "mineral-strip"
end
gaps: The position, size and colours live in the component's own stylesheet, which the contract cannot check: only the markup is evaluated. The React build must ship an equivalent stylesheet (the `.mineral-strip` rules) for the strip to show at all.
It reads `--color-<mineral>` custom properties each site defines in its own global.css; the registry does not ship them.
It takes no props: the Astro runner reads a missing `interface Props` as attribute pass-through, so the prop list says `...attributes` (type never) rather than an empty list.
Fixed to the left edge with no reserved space: content that reaches the edge sits under it.
